Dirichlet prior

Source: R/priors.R
prior_dirichlet.Rd

A Dirichlet distribution for a vector of probabilities that sum to one, such as the frequencies of the test result profiles. It generalizes the Beta distribution to more than two components: each component is Beta distributed on its own.

Usage

prior_dirichlet(concentration = 1)

Arguments

concentration

Concentration parameters, positive finite numbers. Either a single number, repeated for every component, or a numeric vector with one value per component (one per response profile, so its length is 1 or \(J = 2^K\), where \(K\) is the number of tests). The length is checked when the prior is given to a model. Default 1, the uniform distribution on the simplex.

Value

An object of class prior_dirichlet.

Details

Let \(a = (a_1, \dots, a_J)\) be the concentration parameters and \(p = (p_1, \dots, p_J)\), with \(\sum_j p_j = 1\), the vector of probabilities. The distribution has the following properties:

  • the prior mean of component \(j\) is \(a_j / \sum_k a_k\);

  • the total \(\sum_k a_k\) acts as a prior sample size: the larger it is, the more concentrated the distribution is around its mean, while a small total leaves the probabilities widely spread;

  • each component has marginal distribution \(\mathrm{Beta}(a_j, \sum_k a_k - a_j)\).

A single value \(c\) repeated for all components gives a symmetric prior with mean \(1/J\) for every component. With all concentrations equal to 1 the distribution is uniform on the simplex of probabilities. Concentrations below 1 move the mass towards the corners of the simplex, where some components are close to zero; larger concentrations move it towards the prior mean.

Examples

prior_dirichlet(1)
#> <prior_dirichlet> Dirichlet(concentration = 1)
#>   acts on a vector of probabilities
prior_dirichlet(c(2, 1, 1, 1))
#> <prior_dirichlet> Dirichlet(concentration = 2, 1, 1, 1)
#>   acts on a vector of probabilities
